100 Years Ago Today, This is What Was Happening ...

On August 7, 1926, the world was buzzing with significant developments. In Britain, the government faced rising tensions as miners continued their strike for better wages and working conditions, leading to widespread unrest. Meanwhile, in the United States, the nation celebrated the recent passage of the Federal Radio Commission Act, which promised to regulate the burgeoning radio industry. Additionally, the French government announced plans to bolster its military presence in the Rhineland amid ongoing concerns over Germany's recovery post-World War I.
